From e9e3d31d2c141af15518ce6578ef26480fe97878 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2016 19:21:56 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] Allow 16M send/recv blocks

Fix an off by one error introduced by fcff0f3 which triggers an
assertion when 16M blocks are used with send/recv.  This fix was
intentionally not folder in to the Illumos commit so it can be
easily cherry-picked by upstream.

Signed-off-by: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>

diff --git a/module/zfs/bqueue.c b/module/zfs/bqueue.c
index 1ddc697b5..89655cf53 100644
--- a/module/zfs/bqueue.c
+++ b/module/zfs/bqueue.c
@@ -69,7 +69,7 @@ void
 bqueue_enqueue(bqueue_t *q, void *data, uint64_t item_size)
 {
 	ASSERT3U(item_size, >, 0);
-	ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
+	ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
 	mutex_enter(&q->bq_lock);
 	obj2node(q, data)->bqn_size = item_size;
 	while (q->bq_size + item_size > q->bq_maxsize) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `module/zfs/bqueue.c`**
   - The assertion that checks the size of the item being enqueued has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```c
     ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
     ```
   - This change allows for the item size to be equal to the maximum size (`bq_maxsize`), fixing an off-by-one error that caused an assertion failure when using 16M blocks.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `bqueue.c` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of block sizes during send/recv operations. By changing the assertion from a strict less-than (`<`) to a less-than-or-equal-to (`<=`), the code now correctly accommodates the maximum block size of 16M, which was previously causing an assertion failure. This fix is crucial for ensuring that the system can handle the intended maximum block size without triggering errors, thereby improving the robustness of the send/recv functionality.

- `ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);`
- `while (q->bq_size + item_size > q->bq_maxsize) {`

Reason:
The assertion only allowed item sizes that were strictly less than the maximum size (`bq_maxsize`), which caused assertion failures when attempting to enqueue items that were exactly equal to the maximum size (16M blocks). This off-by-one error meant that valid item sizes were incorrectly rejected.

- `+	ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);`

Reason:
The fix changes the assertion to allow item sizes that are less than or equal to the maximum size (`bq_maxsize`). This adjustment prevents assertion failures for valid item sizes, including the edge case of 16M blocks, thus resolving the bug.
